candidates.statement: Order service returns HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders, which the gateway surfaces as 502 on POST /v1/checkout. Traces and logs show every checkout failure paired with a 500 from order within milliseconds, so the gateway is propagating a downstream server error rather than failing itself.
candidates.uncertainty: No order-service telemetry is present, so the internal cause of the order 500 (db, payment, inventory) is not established; only the propagation path is bounded.

report.explanation: Gateway checkout 502s are consistently paired with order-service 500s in traces and logs, with short durations ruling out gateway-side latency. Root cause is bounded to an order-service server error; the specific internal fault needs order-side evidence.
missing_evidence: Order-service traces/logs for POST /v1/orders to identify the internal 500 cause
Order-service dependency metrics (postgresql, payment, inventory) during the incident window
